title: Redwood All-Hands - September 2025
summary: Leadership update covering Q3 performance, product roadmap (Dedicated + Private progress), security/compliance milestones, hiring priorities, and company OKRs. Town-hall Q&A and next steps including deck share and follow-ups on security docs and pilot onboarding.
next_steps: Share Q3 metrics deck with company by EOD 2025-09-11
Security team to publish SOC2 certification FAQ and KMS integration guide by 2025-09-18
Product to open sign-ups for new Dedicated pilot; SEs to coordinate onboarding calls with pilot customers
People Ops to share hiring priorities and interview rubrics week of 2025-09-15
action_items: Ethan Kim: publish benchmark summary for 8k token latency improvements; due 2025-09-17
Priya Singh: finalize Dedicated product rollout timeline; due 2025-09-19
Liam O'Connor: coordinate enterprise sales playbook updates; due 2025-09-16
Security (Anita R): upload SOC2 scoping docs and KMS integration notes; due 2025-09-18
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya P., Ethan K., Priya S., Liam O., company-wide attendees (Q&A at the end)

[00:00:00] Maya Patel: ok hey everyone, welcome to our September all hands, um yeah thanks for joining, I know it's, you know, busy time. quick agenda — top-line metrics, product roadmap, security/compliance update, hiring/org changes and then q and a.

[00:00:16] Maya Patel: quick shoutout before we start — engineering shipped the new batching path for the runtime, that was a big cross-team effort, thank you.

[00:00:30] Ethan Kim: yea thanks team, big props. the new continuous batching and kernel selector changes dropped last week, we're seeing median p50 token latency improvements for 8k contexts in our internal tests, uh roughly 12-18% depending on model variant, it's early but promising. some of the telemetry is a little noisy so we're still validating.

[00:00:55] Priya Singh: and from product side, this lines up with the rollout plan — we're going to feature flag the new runtime optimizations for hosted first then open up to Dedicated nodes. we're planning a staged rollout, canary to 10% traffic then bump.

[00:01:12] Liam O'Connor: on the sales front, that latency story is resonating with a few pilot customers — we had a long discussion with a fintech prospect yesterday who cares a lot about steady tail latency and auditability.

[00:01:28] Speaker 1 (Employee): quick Q — is the Dedicated GA still on track for H2?

[00:01:33] Priya Singh: yes GA for Dedicated is still targeted for late Q4. there's some nuance: the initial GA will support a subset of model sizes and autoscaling policies; full feature parity will follow. we'll share the docs next week.

[00:01:48] Maya Patel: ok next, numbers. high level — ARR growth flat-ish sequentially, but usage per customer up 22% month over month for shipped features, retention steady. we have runway into mid-2027 assuming current spend profile.

[00:02:12] Ethan Kim: a note on infrastructure cost: the kernel selector changes should shave about 8-10% off GPU token cost in some workloads once the Dedicated capacity path is optimized. this is part of our Redwood Optimize tooling work too.

[00:02:28] Priya Singh: product roadmap highlights — Private (VPC/on-prem) alpha is in a handful of customer trials, the feedback so far is around install simplicity and KMS integration. security team has been busy.

[00:02:44] Maya Patel: security update? Anita is on PTO but she shared a note.

[00:02:49] Ethan Kim: sure. short version: SOC 2 readiness is progressing, we expect to submit for audit by end of Q4. we've consolidated audit logs into our central store and are working on retention policies. KMS/HSM integrations for Private are in internal tests; there's still work around SAML SSO flows and RBAC mapping for some enterprise IdPs.

[00:03:15] Speaker 2 (Employee): will SOC 2 cover Dedicated and Private or just hosted?

[00:03:20] Maya Patel: the intention is to cover Redwood's control plane and hosted offerings; for Dedicated/Private we'll have scoped attestations and customer-specific controls — full details in the FAQ Anita will publish.

[00:03:34] Priya Singh: ops note — rollouts will include automated fallback policies, so if a Dedicated pool is degraded we can route to hosted variants with comparable model family. that is a big reliability win for customers who need graceful degradation.

[00:03:50] Ethan Kim: quick tech deep-dive highlight: KV cache changes reduced repeated prefix cost for chat-heavy workloads; we saw 25% fewer redundant pops in a set of internal evals. some transcripts mis-attribute a few tokens but overall quality is stable.

[00:04:08] Maya Patel: hiring/org changes — we've hired a head of reliability (welcome to Jordan Lee, joining next month), and we're increasing hiring for SEs and SREs. People Ops will share the priority list and interview rubrics.

[00:04:24] Liam O'Connor: commercial update — we've closed three mid-market customers this quarter and have two enterprise pilots in flight. the pipeline for Dedicated pilots is healthy, and a couple of prospects are asking for on-prem proof-of-concept.

[00:04:39] Speaker 3 (Employee): can we get more detail on pricing for Dedicated?

[00:04:43] Maya Patel: we'll publish a pricing baseline next week; Liam and finance are finalizing the commit tiers. price will be a combination of reserved GPU capacity + overage and per-token deltas for managed features.

[00:04:58] Ethan Kim: technical note on Private: on-prem packaging is looking good but install time can vary — we're working to automate the k8s manifests and provide a one-click installer for common distros. expect a beta in October.

[00:05:15] Priya Singh: roadmap timeline bullets: Dedicated GA late Q4, Private beta Oct-Nov, Redwood Optimize v1 (batching/caching autosuggestions) in early Q1.

[00:05:28] Maya Patel: culture & org — a reminder about the offsite in November, please RSVP. also feedback from our last engagement survey: folks asked for clearer career ladders and async comms. management will publish updated ladders by end of the month.

[00:05:44] Speaker 4 (Employee): any changes to time off policy or comp banding?

[00:05:48] Maya Patel: no immediate changes to comp bands this quarter; People Ops will run market comps in October. PTO policy remains the same but we're clarifying parental leave and volunteering time in the handbook.

[00:06:00] Liam O'Connor: back to customers — ask for all SEs to flag pilot-ready customers in CRM, I'll send a spreadsheet.

[00:06:10] Priya Singh: quick product demo note — we're adding model catalog metadata (quantization level, verified latency) into the API catalog so customers can pick variants more predictably.

[00:06:22] Speaker 5 (Employee): will the model catalog include per-region availability?

[00:06:25] Ethan Kim: yes, initially for hosted regions, then for Dedicated pools we'll tag pool regions and capacity. sometimes the transcriber mis-heard region names so double-check docs for exact region lists.

[00:06:38] Maya Patel: ok Q&A open. please use the raise hand or chat.

[00:06:45] Speaker 6 (Employee): what are the top risks leadership is tracking?

[00:06:50] Maya Patel: top risks — 1) infrastructure cost creep if batch optimizations lag, 2) sales cycles for Dedicated take longer than expected, 3) compliance timelines — if SOC2 audit slips it affects some enterprise deals. mitigations: cost metrics dashboard, tighter pilot SLAs, and focused security resourcing.

[00:07:12] Speaker 7 (Employee): any customer stories to share?

[00:07:15] Liam O'Connor: yes a retail customer moved a recommender inference to Redwood Dedicated pilot and saw latency tail improvements; we need a case study, we'll get marketing on it.

[00:07:27] Maya Patel: gentle reminder — please annotate PRDs and RFCs with owner and impact, we've had a few docs with stale owners.

[00:07:36] Speaker 8 (Employee): question about troubleshooting — where do SEs surface weird model regressions?

[00:07:40] Priya Singh: there's a shared channel #model-regressions and a template to file an eval run; include prompt set, model hash, and metric diffs. we'll triage within 48 hours.

[00:07:54] Maya Patel: final notes — again big thanks for shipping recent runtime changes; we need to keep shipping and measuring. please read the Q3 metrics deck when it's posted and give feedback.

[00:08:06] Maya Patel: recap of next steps: product to publish rollout docs, security to publish SOC2 FAQ, SEs to flag pilot customers, People Ops to publish hiring priorities. action items will be in the followup email.

[00:08:22] Speaker 9 (Employee): thanks, quick shoutout to infra for handling the incident last week — it was smooth in the end.

[00:08:28] Ethan Kim: yeah huge kudos to on-call.

[00:08:32] Maya Patel: okay we'll wrap. thanks everyone.

[00:08:36] End of recording: meeting concluded at ~10:50 AM PT.
